learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the capacity for analysis and synthesis.
Acquire the capacity for effective problem-solving.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Develop the capacity to transmit information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialized and non-specialized audiences.
Information search and management skills.
Possess the capacity for decision-making.
Develop critical reasoning.
Develop the capacity for teamwork.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Develop the capacity for adaptation to new situations.
Become aware of issues related to the environment.
Knowledge applied to thermal engineering.

Ability to write and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering for the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Capacity for the interpretation of projects and technical reports.
Analyze thermodynamically the fundamental cycles and processes involved in thermal engines, combustion, refrigeration, and air conditioning.
Distinguish and solve basic heat transfer problems by conduction, convection, and radiation.
Solve practical cases of calculation for industrial power production, heat, and industrial cold installations.
Develop competencies related to problem-solving, critical reasoning, teamwork, technical communication, and autonomous learning.
Understand the importance of energy management and energy efficiency in industry and its environmental and economic implications.
Handle classic bibliography, information sources, and new technologies applied to Thermodynamics and Heat Transfer.
Integrate the knowledge acquired in the course with other subjects in the industrial and energy field, fostering an applied and multidisciplinary vision of engineering.

syllabus_topics: BLOCK I: ENERGY AND EXERGY ANALYSIS OF POWER PRODUCTION, COLD PRODUCTION, AND COGENERATION SYSTEMS
BLOCK II: HEATING AND AIR CONDITIONING SYSTEMS
MIXTURES OF IDEAL GASES. HUMID AIR. PSYCHROMETRIC PROCESSES
assessment_rules: The continuous evaluation includes two theoretical-practical tests (35% each, minimum 5/10, recoverable), a practical EES test (20%, no minimum, not recoverable), and continuous assessment tests (10%, 85% completion required, no minimum). If a student scores 5.0 overall but fails a minimum, the final grade will be 4.9. For exceptional evaluation, including exchange students, the weights are 40% for each theoretical-practical test (minimum 5/10, recoverable) and 20% for the practical EES test (no minimum).
